// ============================================================
// A miniature Common.txt for the golden compilation test.
// Written to exercise every shape the compiler recognises, and
// three it must refuse.
// ============================================================

= 13. Compound Adjectives

ALWAYS hyphenate the following:

  non-zero, non-empty, well-defined

NEVER write these without hyphens.

= 14. Forbidden Words and Phrases

The following are NEVER used:

  "clearly" — forbidden
  "so" — NEVER write "so" to connect logical steps.
  ALWAYS write "so" only in fixed phrases: "and so on",
  "do so". In all other contexts NEVER write "so".

= 15. Proof Language

== 15.2 Logical Transitions Within a Proof

[MOVED] Owned by Proof_Style.txt Section 3.2. This section
formerly mandated ALWAYS "Therefore" for every intermediate
step — NEVER "Then". That rule is withdrawn.

= 16. Positive vs. Non-Negative

"positive" — ALWAYS means strictly greater than zero.
NEVER use "positive" to mean $x >= 0$.

= 17. Theorem and Definition Names

ALWAYS write theorem names in full.

  Mean Value Theorem — NEVER MVT

= 18. Miscellaneous Language Rules

"that is" — ALWAYS in full. NEVER "i.e." or "i.e"

= 2. Set Theory

ALWAYS use $subset.eq$ — NEVER $subset$.
